title: 6 Big Intel, AMD And Nvidia AI Data Center Announcements At OCP 2026
key_facts: Intel said its 480 GB "Crescent Island" inference GPU will be the Intel GPU D-series: up to 1.3 petaflops of 8-bit compute in 350 watts, sampling now.
Intel showed server racks with more than 46,000 Xeon 6+ cores.
AMD revealed an open "Helion" rack design and a 192-core EPYC "Verano" chip, entering production in the first half of 2027.
Nvidia open-sourced data-centre software including Run:ai and contributed MGX 1.2 rack designs.
CRN's spec comparison puts Nvidia's RTX Pro 6000 ahead on 8-bit speed while Intel offers far more memory.
Organisers said a record 15,000 people reportedly attended.
quote_evidence: Intel revealed that its upcoming 480-GB “Crescent Island” data center GPU for AI inference will be known as the Intel GPU D-series and feature up to 1.3 petaflops of 8-bit floating-point compute within a 350-watt power envelope.
Verano will enter production in the first half of 2027, according to Su.
why_it_matters_hint: Intel and AMD are pushing to challenge Nvidia as AI data centres add CPUs and open designs.
notes: Company claims; CRN adds its own comparison.
